title: Vector Search Basics
text: Vector search finds semantically similar text by placing it near the query in vector space. It can retrieve by meaning even when keywords differ.
reader_hint: Check whether the question meaning and document keywords both match

title: Keyword Search and Semantic Search
text: Keyword search first checks whether the same words appear, while semantic search compares whether the question and document meanings are close. This can retrieve related documents even when wording differs.
reader_hint: Compare lexical matching with semantic matching

title: Embeddings and Similarity
text: An embedding turns text into a numeric vector, and a similarity calculation compares how close the question vector is to each document vector.
reader_hint: Support the vector and similarity terminology

title: RAG Retrieval Stage
text: In RAG, the system first retrieves relevant documents, attaches those documents to the generation input, and then produces an answer. Retrieval and generation should be inspected separately.
reader_hint: Explain the split between retrieval and generation

title: Document Evidence and Answer Scope
text: Retrieved documents define the evidence boundary an answer should not exceed. Asserting content that is not in the documents is overclaiming at the generation stage.
reader_hint: Boundary document for detecting generation overclaiming

title: Freshness and Retrieval
text: Retrieval can help attach current documents, but retrieved results do not always guarantee current information or correct answers.
reader_hint: Document that blocks the overclaim that retrieval always guarantees freshness

title: Handling Synonym Questions
text: Even when users ask with different wording
category: embedding-based retrieval can raise documents with close meaning as candidates.
column7: Explain expression differences and retrieval recall

title: Checking Top-k Candidates
text: When evaluating retrieval quality
category: do not look only at the final answer; first check which documents were attached as top-k candidates.

title: Irrelevant Document Contamination
text: If search terms are broad or noisy
category: irrelevant documents can enter the candidate set. The generated answer can then become contaminated as well.
column7: Boundary document for retrieval failure spreading into generation

title: Search Term Design
text: Search terms should carry the core meaning of the question. Decorative words or task-irrelevant words can destabilize candidate quality.

title: Recording Evidence Document Titles
text: When reviewing a RAG answer
category: keeping the used document titles and retrieval scores along with the answer makes root-cause tracing easier.
column7: Explain why document titles should be recorded

title: Separating Retrieval Failure and Generation Failure
text: When an answer is wrong, inspect separately whether the retrieved documents were wrong or whether the documents were right but generation overclaimed.
reader_hint: Criterion document for reading retrieval records and answer text separately

title: Query Rewriting
text: When a question is ambiguous
category: rewriting it more specifically before retrieval can help.
column7: Support document for handling ambiguous questions

title: Document Chunk Size
text: If chunks are too large, needed evidence can be buried; if chunks are too small, surrounding context can disappear.

title: Citation Display
text: If the generated answer records which documents it used
category: the user can recheck the evidence.

title: Policy Document Retrieval
text: Policy questions need current policy documents, exception conditions, and effective dates to define the answer scope.

title: Customer Support Retrieval
text: In customer support answers, order status, policy documents, and previous support history can be attached together as candidates.

title: Developer Document Retrieval
text: In developer documentation retrieval, version, function name, and error message strongly affect candidate quality.
